docs.title: What is normalMagic?
docs.text:
normalMagic is a collection of tools for Blender that offer powerful new modelling workflows and advanced control over mesh normals.

Controlling normals can be essential for creating high quality 3D artwork. Hard surfaces, organic shapes, foliage, hair and fur can benefit from modifying normals. Sometimes it's the only way to get surfaces shading the way you want.

Custom Normals

Most of these tools create or edit custom normals.

Once custom normals exist on a mesh, some default Blender tools/modifiers might not behave as expected. Tools are included to fix situations such as mirroring or beveling but it is something to be aware of.

See this video for more information: Custom Normal Issues

docs.title: Advanced Booleans, perfect normals
docs.text:
• Completely avoid Boolean normal issues with Boolean Pro.
  • Repair normals on previously cut geometry with Repair Boolean Normals.
  • Perform advanced Boolean operations with Boolean Extrude, Boolean Trim and Cut Groove.

docs.title: Seamlessly blend surfaces
docs.text:
• Project positions, normals and UVs with Project to Surface.
  • Merge, cut and weld projected meshes into a surface with Surface Insert.

Convenient auto-masking options means no need for creating and managing vertex groups. Sharp edges can be preserved and transferred.

docs.title: Smooth and Transfer Normals
docs.text:
• Smooth and flatten normals normals to improve shading, achieve good toon lighting or for cheap subsurface scattering effects with Smooth Normals.
  • Transfer and blend normals between unconnected meshes using Normal Transfer.

docs.text:
Many tools share common options. They are listed on this page for reference.

docs.title: Mask Falloff
docs.text: When two sets of data blend together there are often falloff controls. These can be found across normalMagic in tools such as Normal Transfer, Surface Insert and Surface Project.

docs.title: Boundary Edge Expand
docs.text:
Select vertices on the boundary edge and expand selection inwards with a linear falloff.

  • Expand Iterations: How many iterations to expand mask inwards.

docs.title: Boundary Edge Distance
docs.text:
Select vertices based on their distance to a boundary edge with a linear falloff.

  • Start Distance: Distance at which vertices will get a value of 1.
  • End Distance: Distance at which vertices will get a value of 0.

docs.title: Surface Distance
docs.text:
Select vertices based on their distance to the target geometry.

  • Start Distance: Distance at which vertices will get a value of 1.
  • End Distance: Distance at which vertices will get a value of 0.

docs.title: Base Falloff
docs.text: The falloff used for values between 0-1. Here it is being used in Surface Project:

docs.title: Falloff Curve
docs.text: Bias the selection towards 1. Here it is being used in Surface Project:

docs.title: Selection
docs.text:
Often we'll want to limit the effects of modifiers to certain areas. The "Selection" section is the same for many tools. It allows for partial selection and, when normals are stored on face corners, hard boundaries.

  • Vertex Group: Specify a vertex group to limit modifier's effect.
  • Face Group (Face Corner Selection Only): Specify a vertex group that will have hard boundaries.
  • Material: Limit the modifier's effect to a specific material.
  • Invert: Invert selection.

Here we can see how Vertex Group and Face Group can be combined:

docs.title: Even Thickness
docs.text:
Many operations involve offsetting the surface of a mesh. These settings will determine how the offset is calculated.

    • None: Points are offset the same distance regardless of face angles.
    • Simple: Distance of offset is limited to attempt even thickness with neighboring faces.
    • Constraints: Distance of offset is projected to attempt even thickness with neighboring faces.

docs.title: Constraints Options
docs.text:
• Clamp Distance: Limit offset distance to a multiple of specified distance. This keeps "explosion error" limited.

  • Boundary: How to offset points on the mesh boundary:

    • Normal: No change in offset direction.
    • Flat: Flatten the offset direction at mesh boundaries.
    • Boundary Angle: Make offset perpendicular to angle of boundary edges. This exposes a setting for how many edges to check to gain an average boundary angle.

    See the "Constraint Boundary Shape" Solidify Pro example in the examples file. .

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
To install normalMagic please see the relevant section for your version:

Base Version is installed as an asset library.

Pro Version is installed as an add-on (that is packaged with the asset library).

docs.title: Base Version (Asset Library)
docs.text:
The Base version of normalMagic is installed as an asset library, not an add-on.

TLDR

Download the .zip, extract to a folder, add the folder as an asset library.

For more detailed instructions see below.

For more information on asset libraries you can check Blender's Official Documentation

docs.title: First Time Install
docs.text:
1. Download latest .zip file for the closest Blender version (normalMagic 4.5 v1.0.blend).
  2. Unzip/extract to a folder in your desired location.
  3. Open Blender and go to Edit/Preferences/Asset Libraries.
  4. Click + Add Asset Library.
  5. Navigate to the unzipped folder and press Add Asset Library.
  6. You should now see "normalMagic" in your asset libraries. Optional: Here you can choose how the data is imported by default. Link keeps scenes up to date with the installed library and reduces file sizes, but files need the library to open. Pack and Append store a copy in each file, so files work anywhere but keep their version until you update them. See the Official Documentation for more information.

normalMagic should now be installed. Modifiers will now show up under the Add Modifier menu:

docs.title: Update Asset Library
docs.text:
To update to a newer version of the normalMagic asset library:

  1. Remove existing asset library under Edit/Preferences/File Paths/Asset Libraries.
  2. Repeat install instructions to add new version.

Alternatively you could replace the files in the existing library with the newer ones.

docs.title: Pro Version (Add-on)
docs.text:
The Pro version of normalMagic is installed as an add-on. The asset library is now packaged with the add-on and can be set up with a single click.

TLDR

  • Download the add-on .zip file and drag it into Blender's viewport.
  • The asset library is set up automatically.

Remove Existing Asset Libraries

Updating from 1.x versions will require removing the existing asset library from Edit/Preference/File Paths/Asset Libraries.

docs.title: Install Add-on
docs.text:
To install/update the add-on simply:

  1. Download the latest "addon" .zip file.
  2. Drag the .zip file into Blender and press OK.
  3. The bundled asset library is set up automatically. If it isn't found, press Install Asset Library in the sidebar, or Open Preferences to use an asset library from elsewhere (See the next section).

Other normalMagic Libraries

If you have other normalMagic asset libraries installed (e.g. the Base version or a 1.x version), they are listed in the add-on's preferences where you can disable or remove them.

docs.title: Custom Asset Library Location
docs.text:
It is advised to use the asset library bundled with the add-on to keep them in sync. However, if you want your asset library imported from another location follow the instructions below.

  1. Add the asset library through Edit/Preferences/File Paths/Asset Libraries (see Base Version instructions).
  2. In the add-on's preferences, set Location to Custom and choose your library from the list.

Library Version

A custom library won't update with the add-on. The add-on will warn you if the library's version doesn't match.

docs.title: Update Add-on
docs.text:
1. Drag the new .zip file into Blender, this will update the existing version.
  2. The bundled asset library updates with the add-on. If you are using a custom asset library location this will need updating manually.

Your preferences and Modifier Defaults are kept when updating.

docs.title: Update Existing Scenes
docs.text: Modifiers that already exist in scenes might need updating depending on your asset library setup.

docs.title: Pro Add-on
docs.text:
The add-on detects normalMagic modifiers made with an older version.

When opening an older file a Newer Modifiers Available message shows at the top of the sidebar panel, and an info dropdown shows in the modifier header.

  • Update Packed Modifiers. Replace old modifiers with the versions from the current asset library. With the Linked import method you can choose Update & Link or Update Packed instead.
  • Ignore, Keep Old Versions. Keep the old versions in this file. You'll be asked again when a newer version of normalMagic is installed.

Modifier settings are kept when updating. Updating can be undone with Ctrl+Z.

Breaking Changes

If a modifier has changed in a way that may affect how existing scenes look, a Breaking Changes dialog lists those modifiers before updating. Untick any you want to keep at their old version.

To turn off update checks, disable Offer to Update Existing Modifiers in the preferences.

docs.title: Base Version
docs.text: For the Base version (asset library only), update modifiers manually.

docs.title: Linked Library
docs.text:
If library is set to "Link", modifiers update automatically when the new version is installed in the same location.

If the new version is installed somewhere else, point existing scenes to it:

  1. Go to the outliner and change the view to "Blend File".
  2. Locate the normalMagic file.
  3. Right Click/Relocate.
  4. Select .blend file in the current asset library path.

docs.title: Packed/Appended Library
docs.text:
Update modifiers in existing scenes if library is set to "Pack" or "Append". These store a copy in each file, which doesn't update when the library does:

  1. Add new version of modifier somewhere in your scene.
  2. Go to the outliner and change the view to "Blend File".
  3. Find the old modifier:
    • Appended: under "Node Groups".
    • Packed: under the normalMagic library it was packed from (not under "Node Groups").
  4. Right Click/Remap Users.
  5. Select the newer version:
    • Appended: most likely called ".001".
    • Packed: same name, from the newer normalMagic library.

docs.title: Tools Overview
docs.text:
Custom Normals

Most of these tools create or edit custom normals. These can be unintuitive to work with if you're unfamiliar with them.

Once custom normals exist on a mesh, some default Blender tools/modifiers might not behave as expected. Tools are included to fix situations such as mirroring or beveling but it is something to be aware of.

docs.title: Pro Add-on
docs.text:
The Pro add-on is the fastest way to work with normalMagic:

  • Set up modifiers, cutters and inserts in one click.
  • Manage complex scenes with modifier/object dependencies.
  • Work destructively without worrying about custom normal types.
  • Use checkpoints to keep working with heavy modifier stacks without slowdown.
Add-on features

  • Boolean Pro

    Select cutters, then the object, and click. Cutters are set up for you.

  • Surface Integration

    Insert or project meshes onto a surface in one click.

  • Modifier References

    Show, hide, select or apply every object your modifiers reference.

  • Instance Objects

    Duplicate as instances, or use checkpoints to keep heavy stacks responsive.

  • Object Display

    Make cutters and helpers "Viewport Only" so they never show in renders.

  • Modifier Header

    Add common modifiers from a button bar above the modifier stack.

  • Modifier Defaults

    Save your preferred settings for any modifier. Kept through updates.

  • Free Normals Warnings

    Get warned before edits or deformation break custom normals, with one-click fixes.

docs.title: Asset Library
docs.text: The core of normalMagic is an asset library of modifiers. You'll also find all of these tools in the sidebar.

docs.title: Mesh Modifiers
docs.text:
These modifiers affect normals, underlying geometry and other attributes such as UVs.

  • Boolean Pro

    Replacement for Blender's built-in Boolean modifier with extra options and accurate normals.

  • Boolean Trim

    Cut and 'Trim' a mesh using single-sided cutter objects.

  • Boolean Extrude

    Cuts and extrudes where cutter meshes intersect.

  • Project to Surface

    Project and blend geometry onto other mesh surfaces.

  • Surface Insert

    Project, cut, blend and weld insert meshes into the surface of a mesh.

  • Symmetrize

    Single axis mirror with extra options that works with custom normals.

  • Solidify Pro

    Solidify meshes with advanced profile control. Supports custom normals.

  • Offset Surface

    Offset the surface of a mesh with options for even thickness.

  • Cut Groove

    Cut a v-shaped groove or gap into a surface where cutter objects intersect.

docs.title: Normal Modifiers
docs.text:
These modifiers affect the normals of a mesh and nothing else.

  • Normal Transfer

    Transfer normals from other mesh objects.

  • Smooth Normals

    Smooth normals without smoothing mesh topology.

  • Face Weighted Normals

    Face weighted normals with selection control.

  • Bent Normals

    Calculate bent normals directly on geometry for better ambient lighting.

  • Repair Bevel Normals

    Fix the normals of bevels on meshes with custom normals.

  • Repair Boolean Normals

    Fix bad normals caused by applied Booleans.

  • Repair Mirrored Normals

    Flip custom normals on mirrored geometry so they point the right way.

  • Lock Normals

    Create custom normals, or convert between "Free" and "Tangent Space" normals.

docs.title: Visualize Modifiers
docs.text:
These modifiers produce geometry to visualize normals and related attributes.

  • View Normals

    Visualize mesh normals in the viewport.

  • View Sharp

    Visualize sharp edges in the viewport.

docs.title: Other Modifiers
docs.text:
These modifiers change things related to normals, such as sharp edges or face orientation.

  • Instance Object

    Instance another object to replace or append to the current geometry.

  • Mark Sharp

    Mark sharp edges by angle, with options to add or remove custom normals.

  • Sharp Edges to Attribute

    Write edge and point attributes based on sharp edges.

  • Auto-Flip Faces

    Detect and fix flipped faces automatically.

  • Change Materials

    Assign materials or material indices to face selections.

docs.title: Manual Tools
docs.text:
These tools are available as destructive operations. There isn't much here yet, if you wish to see more modifiers become manual tools please reach out!

  • Recalculate Normals

    Weighted normals and mark sharp for selected geometry in Edit Mode.

  • Add Custom Normals

    Add custom normals to selected mesh objects.
