docs.text:
The "Advanced Booleans" section lets you add the following modifiers:

  • Boolean Extrude
  • Boolean Trim
  • Cut Groove

docs.title: Modifier Settings
docs.text: To change the default settings for any modifier, use the Modifier Defaults menu to save defaults from a modifier.

docs.title: Cutter Behavior
docs.text:
This section lets you choose what happens to objects when you add a Boolean.

  • Display As. Change the display mode of the cutter object:

    • Wireframe. Display cutter as wireframe.
    • Bounds. Display cutter as bounding box.

  • Collection. When enabled, specify the name of a collection to add cutter objects to. Each scene keeps its own cutter collection, which is reused by name. If it doesn't exist one will be created.

  • Deselect. Which objects get deselected after the Boolean operation:
    • None. Keep all objects selected.
    • Main Object. Deselect the object that receives the modifier.
    • Cutters. Deselect cutter object(s)
  • Parent to Object. Parent the cutter object(s) to the main object. This will transform them together when you move the main object.
  • Link Split Mesh. When performing the Split operation, link the intersected mesh to the original so editing one mesh edits the other too.
  • Auto-Smooth. Apply the Preferred Smooth Modifier to objects in Boolean operation if they don't have one already. Instances and checkpoints are skipped, as their shading comes from the source object:
    • Cutters. Apply smoothing to cutter object(s).
    • All. (Default) Apply smoothing to all objects involved in the Boolean.
    • None. Don't apply smoothing to any objects.
  • Angle. Angle to set auto-smoothing at when "Auto-Smooth" is turned on.

docs.title: Convert Existing Booleans
docs.text:
Will convert all 'Boolean' modifiers on selected objects to 'Boolean Pro'. All relevant settings will be transferred, along with the modifier's name, on/off toggles and position in the stack. Collection Booleans are converted using Boolean Pro's Collection mode.

The Convert Existing Booleans button shows at the bottom of the panel when any selected object has a Blender Boolean modifier. You can also search for it with the F3 operator search:

docs.title: Free Normals Warnings
docs.text:
Blender can store custom normals in two ways:

  • Free. Fast, and what normalMagic modifiers create by default. These don't follow later edits or deformation.
  • Tangent. Slower, but they follow edits and deformation.

There are two main areas where "Free" normals can cause problems:

  1. When they exist on the source mesh data, edits will break the normals.
  2. When stacking deforming modifiers after normalMagic ones, the normals won't follow the deformations.

The add-on shows a warning for both cases.

Applying Modifiers

When applying modifiers from the Modifier References panel, "Free" normals are converted to tangent normals automatically.

docs.title: Source Normals Warning
docs.text:
When the mesh data of selected objects stores "Free" custom normals, a " Free Normals" menu shows at the end of the tool header, in Edit Mode and Object Mode.

  • Convert to Tangent Normals. (Recommended) Converts the stored normals to tangent normals.
  • Don't Warn in This Scene. Hide this warning for the current scene.

To hide this warning everywhere, turn off "Warn About Free Source Normals" in preferences.

docs.title: Deform Warning
docs.text:
When "Free" normals reach a deforming modifier (e.g. Armature, Lattice, Simple Deform), a "" dropdown shows at the end of the modifier header.

  • Convert With Lock Normals Modifier. Adds a Lock Normals modifier set to "Tangent" before the deforming modifier.
  • Ignore in This Scene. Hide this warning for the current scene.

Turning Warnings Back On

Warnings hidden for a scene can be turned back on in preferences.

docs.title: Instance Objects
docs.text: These tools make it easier to use the Instance Object modifier.

docs.title: Duplicate Instanced
docs.text:
This operator that acts like Blender's built-in Duplicate Linked but also copies the results of all modifiers:

The instanced object can be duplicated with any existing methods e.g. Shift+D and will keep the same behavior.

Using this operator on an object that already is using a "Instance Object" as it's last modifier will instance the original object to keep things simple.

Toggle the button next to the operator to start moving the instance straight away.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
For each selected object:

  1. Create a new object with the same mesh data as selected object. This is so you can still enter "Edit Mode" on the instance.
  2. Add Instance Object modifier and specify selected object.
  3. Select instance object and deselect original.

docs.title: Checkpoints
docs.text:
Checkpoints are an alternative to large modifier stacks. Create a checkpoint to "freeze" the result of an object's modifiers into an instance, then keep adding modifiers to the checkpoint. Changing modifiers on the checkpoint doesn't re-evaluate the source object's modifiers, so they stay interactive, and you can always step back to change earlier modifiers.

  • Create Checkpoint. Instance the selected object(s) as a checkpoint named <source>_checkpoint_<n>, with an Instance Object modifier named <source> checkpoint <n>. Creating a checkpoint from the last checkpoint continues the chain.
  • / Previous/Next. Step along the chain from the active object. Previous goes to the object the checkpoint instances, back to the original source. Next goes to the checkpoint made from it. The object you step to is shown and selected, and the current one is hidden (in the viewport and in renders). Needs a selected mesh or curve. Checkpoints hidden by their collection are revealed through the Hidden Collections dialog.
  • Checkpoint Settings (dropdown):
    • Parent to Source. (Off by default) Parent checkpoint objects to the original source object.
    • Hide Source. (On by default) Hide the object a checkpoint is made from, in the viewport and in renders.

docs.title: Branches
docs.text:
Creating a checkpoint from an object that already has one after it (e.g. stepping back with Previous and creating a new checkpoint) starts a branch. A dialog asks you to confirm first. Duplicating a checkpoint with Shift+D also creates a branch.

When there is more than one branch, Next goes to the newest checkpoint.

docs.title: Collapsing Checkpoints
docs.text: A checkpoint is part of the chain while its Instance Object modifier is first in the stack. If you apply that modifier (e.g. with Collapse to Selected), the checkpoint becomes a normal object: Previous and Select Source no longer go back past it, and checkpoints made from it start a new chain.

docs.title: Select Source
docs.text:
Selects the source object(s) being instanced by selected object(s). This is useful when you wish to edit the mesh or change modifiers on the original object.

  • On a checkpoint, selects the original source object of the chain.
  • Show Source. (On by default) If the source object is hidden, it is unhidden. If it's hidden by its collection, the Hidden Collections dialog asks before turning the collection on.

docs.title: Modifier Defaults
docs.text:
You can save default settings for any modifier added via normalMagic operators.

Note

This will have no effect on modifiers added through the "Add Modifier" menu.

This is achieved through the Modifier Defaults menu, available in the Modifier Header bar and the Modifier References panel.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
The menu acts on the active (highlighted) modifier:

  • Save Defaults. Save all settings from the active modifier and use them as the default. In Blender 5.2+ output attribute names are saved too.
  • Restore Defaults. Set the active modifier's settings back to your saved defaults, or the built-in defaults if none are saved. Object and collection inputs (and Boolean Pro's operation) are kept.
  • Delete Custom Defaults. Delete your saved defaults for this modifier. Modifiers added with normalMagic will use the built-in defaults again.

Kept Through Updates

Saved defaults are stored in the add-on's user folder and are kept when you update the add-on. Uninstalling the add-on removes them.

docs.title: Modifier Header
docs.text: The optional modifier header bar gives quick access to several normalMagic features without using the sidebar. From left to right:

docs.title: Expand Arrow
docs.text: Show the Modifier References panel below.

docs.title: Operators Bar
docs.text:
A row of buttons for quickly adding normalMagic operators. These can configured in preferences.

All of these allow for multi-object selection, for assigning cutters for example. Modifiers added from the header bar only collapse their object inputs panel (when objects are assigned) so the rest of the settings stay visible.

Available buttons:

  • Mark Sharp
  • Symmetrize
  • Solidify Pro
  • Bevel. Adds Blender's Bevel modifier with Face Strength set to "All", followed by a Repair Bevel Normals modifier.
  • Smooth Normals
  • Face Weighted Normals
  • Normal Transfer. Works like Project to Surface: other selected objects get a Normal Transfer modifier that transfers normals from the active object.
  • Boolean Pro: Difference, Union, Intersect, Slice and Split
  • Boolean Extrude, Boolean Trim and Cut Groove
  • Surface Insert and Project to Surface

docs.title: Modifier Defaults
docs.text: Save, restore or delete the default settings for the active modifier. These will be used any time a modifier of the same type is added via the add-on. See here for more info.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
Small dropdowns appear at the end of the header bar when something needs attention:

  • Node Updates. Newer versions of normalMagic modifiers on this object are available. See Update Existing Scenes.
  • Free Normals. "Free" custom normals reach a deforming modifier. See Free Normals Warnings.

docs.title: Modifier References
docs.text:
Use this panel to manage complex non-destructive scenes with many cutters, inserts, or other objects referenced by modifiers.

Active Object

This panel shows modifiers for the active object only i.e. modifiers that show up in Blender's modifiers panel.

Instantly select, show or hide objects that are referenced by the active object's modifiers.

docs.title: UI Breakdown
docs.text:
The main list displays the active object's modifiers (see Filter References). Selecting a modifier will also select it in the object's modifier panel and display it's individual references below.

  • 1. Hide/Show All: Hide or show all referenced objects for the active object. Filter the modifier list below.

    2. Modifier List: Each entry here is a modifier on the active object: - Toggle modifier - Show/Hide referenced objects - Select/Deselect referenced objects

    3. Modifier Defaults: Set the default settings for the highlighted modifier. See here for more information.

    4. Apply/Remove Modifier: Apply or remove the highlighted modifier with an option to delete referenced objects. See Apply & Delete.

    5. Referenced Objects: Displays referenced objects, you can rename them here.

docs.title: Filter References
docs.text:
The filter dropdown next to Hide/Show All chooses which modifiers show in the list:

  • Without References. (On by default) Show modifiers that don't reference any objects.
  • Checkpoint Source. (Off by default) Show a checkpoint's Instance Object modifier, which references the previous checkpoint. Off by default so Show All doesn't unhide the previous checkpoint.
  • Instance Source. (On by default) Show an instance's Instance Object modifier, which references the object it instances.

Modifiers hidden from the list are skipped by Hide/Show All and Select All.

docs.title: Hidden Collections
docs.text:
Showing or selecting referenced objects also reveals objects that are hidden because of their collection. When this is needed, a Hidden Collections dialog first lists each object and its hidden collections (hidden, excluded, or "Disable in Viewports"). Press Force Show to turn those collections back on.

Warning

Force Show turns on the whole collection, including everything in it. Turning off a collection's "Disable in Viewports" affects every view layer and scene.

The same dialog is used by Select Source and checkpoint Previous/Next.

docs.title: Apply & Delete
docs.text:
These buttons act on the highlighted modifier:

  • Delete Objects on Modifier Apply: Toggle whether referenced objects are deleted when the modifier is applied or removed. The number shows how many objects are referenced.
  • Delete Modifier: Remove the modifier.
  • Apply Single Modifier: Apply only this modifier.
  • Collapse to Selected: Apply all modifiers from the top of the stack down to and including this one.

When applying modifiers:

  • "Free" custom normals are converted to "Tangent" normals (Create Tangent Normals, on by default) so they keep following later edits and deformation. See Free Normals Warnings.
  • Meshes shared with other objects (instances, linked duplicates) are made single user, so other objects aren't affected.

docs.title: Shared References
docs.text:
If an object that would be deleted is also used by another modifier, a Shared References dialog lists those objects and the modifiers using them. Choose to:

  • Keep shared objects: (Default) Only delete objects no other modifier uses.
  • Delete anyway: Delete all referenced objects.

docs.title: Object Display
docs.text:
This panel helps manage object's visibility. Assigning a mesh as Viewport Only will hide it from all renders but keep it visible in the viewport.

This is particularly useful for objects referenced by Mesh Modifiers such as Surface Insert

docs.title: Rendered
docs.text:
Show object in renders and viewport. Applies default "visible" object properties.

Display in viewport as either Wire, Solid (default), or Textured.

docs.title: Viewport Only
docs.text:
Hides object from all renders but keeps it visible in the viewport.

Display in viewport as either Bounds, Wire (default), or Solid.

docs.title: Preferences
docs.text:
These options show up under Edit/Preferences/Add-ons/normalMagic

Kept Through Updates

Preferences and Modifier Defaults are kept when you update the add-on.

docs.title: UI Preferences
docs.text:
• Show Sidebar Panel. Enable/disable the add-on's sidebar panel. Expand to specify it's category (default is "Normal Magic")
  • Show Modifier Header. Enable/disable the modifier header. Expand to choose which add-modifier buttons show in the header.

docs.title: Auto Smooth
docs.text:
• Preferred Smooth Modifier. Which smooth modifier (Mark Sharp or Smooth by Angle) gets added with Boolean Pro's cutter "Auto-Smooth" option and Shade Auto Smooth (First).
  • Shade Auto Smooth (First) in Object Menu. (On by default) Show Shade Auto Smooth (First) in the object right-click menu.

docs.title: Normal Warnings
docs.text:
• Warn About Free Source Normals. Show a warning in the tool header when selected meshes store "Free" custom normals. See Free Normals Warnings.
  • This Scene. Turn hidden warnings back on for the current scene:
    • Hide Free Source Normals Warning.
    • Hide Deform Normals Warning.

docs.title: Asset Library
docs.text:
Shows the asset library the add-on is using, its version and its location. If there is a problem with the library (missing, disabled, or a version that doesn't match the add-on) it is shown here with a button to fix it.

  • Location. Which asset library to add modifiers from:
    • Bundled. (Default, recommended) Use the asset library that comes with the add-on. It is set up automatically when the add-on is installed or updated, so it always matches the add-on's version.
    • Custom. Use one of your own asset libraries. Choose the library from the list, or press Manage Libraries to open Blender's asset library preferences.
  • Import Method. How normalMagic node groups are added to files:
    • Packed. (Default) Pack node groups into each file. Files work anywhere and keep their version until you update them.
    • Linked. Link node groups from the asset library. Files always use the installed version, but need the asset library to open correctly.
  • Offer to Update Existing Modifiers. Show a button to update normalMagic modifiers in files made with an older version. See Update Existing Scenes.

docs.title: Other normalMagic Libraries
docs.text: If other normalMagic asset libraries are installed (for example the Base version or an older version), they are listed here. While enabled, their modifiers will also show up in Blender's "Add Modifier" menu. You can disable them (Blender 5.2+), or remove them from Blender's preferences with the Remove Asset Library button (the files aren't deleted).

docs.title: Surface Integration
docs.text: This panel contains operators to quickly add Surface Insert and Project to Surface modifiers.

docs.title: Surface Insert
docs.text: Add a Surface Insert modifier to the active object.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. (Optional) Select 1-6 insert meshes
  2. Select surface mesh last
  3. Press the Surface Insert button

docs.title: Insert mesh options
docs.text: Similar to the Boolean cutters menu, there are options for what to do with insert meshes.

docs.title: Project to Surface
docs.text: Add a Project to Surface modifier to all selected objects but the last selected.

docs.title: How to Use
docs.text:
1. Select one or more objects you wish to project
  2. Select the surface mesh last
  3. Press the Project to Surface button

Single Surface

By default (Single Surface on) every other selected object projects onto the active (last selected) object. Turn Single Surface off in the "Adjust Last Operation" panel to project the active object onto all other selected objects instead. More than 6 surfaces will add extra modifiers.

docs.title: Projection Mesh Options
docs.text: Similar to the Boolean cutters menu, there are options for what to do with the projected meshes.

docs.title: Modifier Settings
docs.text: To change default modifier settings for either modifier, see modifier defaults.

docs.title: Add Custom Normals
docs.text: Found in the Object menu. Adds custom normals to selected mesh objects. Internally uses the Lock Normals tool.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Normal Type: How to store custom normals:

    • Free: Store custom normals as simple vectors in the local space of the mesh. This is efficient and fast to evaluate but does not support deformation.
    • Tangent Space: Store normals in a deformation dependent custom transformation space. This method is slower, but can be better when subsequent operations change the mesh without handling normals specifically.

  • Normal Domain: When Custom Normal Type is set to Free:

    • Face Corner. Store normals on face corners, allows for sharp edges.
    • Point. Store normals on points, cannot have sharp edges.

docs.title: Recalculate Normals
docs.text:
Found in the Mesh/Normals alt + N menu in "Edit Mode".

Calculates weighted normals and mark sharp for selected geometry. This is a tool version of the Face Weighted Normals and Mark Sharp modifiers.

Normals are stored as "Tangent" custom normals by default, so they follow later edits and deformation. See Lock Normals for the difference between "Free" and "Tangent" normals.

docs.title: Boolean Extrude
docs.text: Cuts and extrudes where cutter meshes intersect.

docs.title: Extrusion Operation
docs.text:
Equal and Opposite

These two operations are essentially the inverse of each other. Duplicating the object and using opposite operations with different outsets can create interesting effects.

docs.title: Emboss
docs.text: Slice mesh and extrude intersection faces in or out.

docs.title: Panel
docs.text: Perform an "Intersect" Boolean and extrude the result into a solid panel.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Please check out the examples file to see Boolean Extrude in action.

docs.title: Cutters
docs.text:
This section specifies which cutters to use.

  • Objects/Collection: Choose individual mesh objects or a collection containing mesh objects.
  • Object Count: How many cutter mesh objects to use (when in Objects mode).
  • Cutter Outset: Expands the cutter mesh with options for even thickness.

docs.title: Extrude
docs.text:
Control the extrude operation.

  • Operation: Choose between Emboss/Panel operations:
    • Emboss Surface: Slice mesh and extrude intersection faces in or out.
    • Panel: Perform an "Intersect" Boolean and extrude the result into a solid panel.
  • Amount: Distance to extrude.
  • Extrusion Method: How to generate extrusion:
    • Extrude Faces: Extrude intersection area(s) along surface normal. The rim is a strip of quads perpendicular to original surface with options to inset the cut area.
    • Offset Boolean: Offset surface and cut with Boolean cutter(s). The rim is aligned to cutter(s) and there are no options to inset the cut area.
  • Offset Even: Use even thickness settings on extrusion.
  • Boolean Solver: Boolean solver to use internally.

docs.title: Inset
docs.text:
(Extrude Faces mode only). Inset the front of the extrude operation.

  • Scale: Scale extruded faces around their average position.
  • Inset: Inset extruded faces away from the extrusion boundary.
  • Edge Falloff: Falloff distance from the edge of the inset. Use to smooth errors at the edge of the inset.

docs.title: Normals
docs.text:
• Transfer Normals: Transfer normals from source geometry. Produces the best normals.
  • Rim Sharp Angle: Mark edges as sharp on the extrusion rim if they exceed this angle.

docs.title: Weld
docs.text: Weld points by distance

docs.title: Boolean Pro
docs.text:
Boolean Pro is designed to act as a replacement for Blender's built-in Boolean modifier that provides extra functionality. For reference, documentation for Blender's built-in modifier can be found here.

Add-on

The normalMagic Add-on includes operators to quickly set up the Boolean Pro modifier, similar to the Bool Tool add-on.

The most powerful feature is transferring the normals automatically from Boolean inputs for perfect Boolean normals:

The cutter object can be given an outset (expanded) with even thickness before cutting:

There is also a Slice operation with optional inset:

Intersect Union Difference Slice

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Be sure to check out the examples file to see Boolean Pro in action.

docs.title: Cutters
docs.text: Specify cutter geometry. You can specify up to 6 objects or use a collection.

docs.title: Cutters
docs.text:
This section specifies which cutters to use.

  • Objects/Collection: Choose individual mesh objects or a collection containing mesh objects.
  • Object Count: How many cutter mesh objects to use (when in Objects mode).
  • Outset: Expands the cutter mesh with options for even thickness.

docs.title: Boolean
docs.text:
• Operation: Which Boolean operation to perform.
    • Intersect: Keep the part of the mesh that is shared between inputs.
    • Union: Combine input meshes into a single mesh.
    • Difference: (Default) Subtract input meshes from source mesh.
    • Slice: Slice source mesh with input meshes. This combines "Intersect" and "Difference" into the same output.
  • Solver:
    • Float: Simple solver with good performance.
    • Exact: Slower solver with best results on coplanar faces.
    • Manifold: (Default) Fastest solver that only works on manifold meshes, but gives better results.
  • Inset (Slice Mode): Offsets the cutter inwards for the intersect Boolean to give a gap between meshes.

docs.title: Weld
docs.text:
• Merge by Distance: Which vertices to merge by distance after the Boolean:
    • None: (Default) Don't merge any vertices.
    • Boundaries Only: Only merge vertices along the Boolean boundary. Use this to clean up small slivers along the cut.
    • All Vertices: Merge all vertices by distance.
  • Distance: Distance at which to merge vertice.

docs.title: Shading
docs.text:
• Materials: How to assign materials to new faces.
    • Index Based: Match material index from Boolean meshes.
    • Specify: Specify a material to apply to all new faces.
    • Transfer: Transfer materials from Boolean meshes. This might not be accurate when using collections.
  • Transfer Normals: Use normals from input meshes. Produces the best normals.
  • Mark Sharp: Mark all intersection edges between meshes as sharp.

docs.title: Solver Options
docs.text:
• Result: Whether to output a solid object or a cut surface.
    • Solid: Output full Boolean result.
    • Surface: Output a cut surface with open edges where new faces would appear.
  • Non-Manifold Fallback: Solver to use when an input isn't manifold:
    • Float: Simple solver with good performance.
    • Exact: Slower solver with best results on coplanar faces.
  • Self Intersection (Exact solver only): Correctly calculates cases when one or both operands have self-intersections. This involves more calculations making the node slower.
  • Hole Tolerant: Optimizes the Boolean output for non-manifold geometry at the cost of increased computational time. Because of the performance impact, this option should only be enabled when the solver demonstrates errors with non-manifold geometry.

docs.title: Boolean Trim
docs.text:
Cut and 'Trim' a mesh using single-sided cutter object(s).

  • Trim plane(s) can turn corners
  • Multiple trim planes can be used with one modifier

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Trim plane(s) must be single sided.
  • Trim plane(s) must extend through the entire mesh.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Please check out the examples file to see Boolean Trim in action.

docs.title: Trim Planes
docs.text:
• Objects/Collection: Choose individual mesh objects or a collection containing mesh objects.
  • Object Count: How many mesh objects to insert (when in Objects mode).

docs.title: Trim
docs.text:
• Reverse Trim Direction. Trim faces on the opposite side of the trim plane(s).
  • Solver. The Boolean solver to use for the trim operation.
  • Un-Sliced Islands. What to do with mesh islands that aren't sliced by the Boolean operation:
    • Trim Per Island. Delete un-sliced mesh islands based on the direction of the nearest cutting plane(s).
    • Keep All. Keep all un-sliced mesh islands.
    • Remove All. Remove all un-sliced mesh islands.
  • Offset. Offset the trim plane(s) with even offset.
  • Result.
    • Solid. Output solid mesh if possible. Trimmed section is filled.
    • Surface. Output single-sided mesh. Trimmed section is removed.

docs.title: Advanced
docs.text: • Plane Extrusion. How much the trim plane is extruded before the Boolean operation.

docs.title: How it Works
docs.text:
1. Trim planes are extruded into solid shapes by a tiny amount in the opposite direction to the trim operation.
  2. These shapes are used for a difference Boolean on the main mesh.
  3. Mesh islands on the trimmed side are deleted.

docs.title: Cut Groove
docs.text: Cut a v-shaped groove or a gap into a surface along the intersection of cutter objects.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
The Cut Groove Modifier performs the following steps:

  1. Generate a curve from the intersection of cutter objects.
  2. Convert the curve to a 'ribbon' mesh that follows the surface closely.
  3. Extrude the 'ribbon' mesh with a v-shaped profile to create a solid 'groove cutter'.
  4. Cut the 'groove cutter' from the original surface using a difference Boolean.

Viewing Steps

You can view the result of each of the above steps using the Debug panel

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Be sure to check out the examples file to see Cut Groove in action.

docs.title: Cut Operation
docs.text:
• Groove: Cut a V-shape channel into geometry where cutters intersect. This should keep meshes manifold.
  • Gap: Cut a gap of even width where cutters intersect. This will create non-manifold geometry.

docs.title: Cutter Objects
docs.text:
This section specifies which cutters to use.

  • Objects/Collection: Choose individual mesh objects or a collection containing mesh objects.
  • Object Count: How many cutter mesh objects to use (when in Objects mode).
  • Cutter Outset: Expands the cutter mesh with options for even thickness.

docs.title: Cutter Geometry
docs.text:
Control how the groove cutter is generated. This can be previewed using the "Final Cutters" debug view.

  • Cutter Alignment: Where the groove sits relative to the cutter:
    • Groove Border: (Default) The Groove's border's are centered on the intersection.
    • Groove Center: The Groove slides until the center point lies on the cutter.
    • Border & Center: Combines both alignments. Sides may be uneven.
  • Width: Width of the cut.
  • Groove/Cutter Depth: How deep to make the cutter.
  • Cutter Boundary Weld: Distance at which to weld points along the cutter boundary. This is useful for avoiding bad shading and mesh errors along the cut boundary.
  • Edge Slide Angle: Slide cutter edges along base mesh edges if they are within this angle.

docs.title: Intersection Curve
docs.text:
Control over the curve generated at cutter intersection. This can be previewed using the "Intersection Curve" debug view.

  • Line Solver: Which Boolean solver to use to generate the curve.
  • Simplify Curve: Remove inline points from curve.
  • Distance Weld: Weld points closer than this threshold.

docs.title: Boolean
docs.text:
Settings for final Boolean where groove mesh is cut into the object's surface.

  • Non-Manifold Solver: Which Boolean solver to use when one or more inputs is not manifold.
  • Merge By Distance: Merge Vertices by distance after Boolean operation.

docs.title: Normals
docs.text:
How to calculate normals.

  • Transfer Normals: Transfer normals with the Boolean operation. It is recommended to keep this on to avoid shading artifacts.
  • Match Boundary Normals: Match the normals on the edge of the groove. This makes the sharp edge appear rounded.
  • Groove Sharp Angle: Angle at which to mark edges as sharp on the groove faces.

docs.title: Groove UVs
docs.text:
For "Groove" operation only.

  • Method: How to generate UVs:
    • Inherit Surface UVs: Project UVs from original surface.
    • UV Strip: Generate new UVs in a strip along the groove.
  • UV Map: UV Map to write to.

docs.title: Debug
docs.text:
This section lets you inspect the steps of the process if the modifier isn't behaving as expected.

  • View. Outputs geometry from different points in the node graph.

    Warning

    This changes the output of the graph, make sure to turn off when you're done inspecting.

    • Intersection Curve: Output the curve generated by the Boolean intersection.
    • Ribbon: Output the extruded curve or "ribbon".
    • Final Cutters: Output the 'groove cutter' extruded from the 'ribbon'.

docs.title: Offset Surface
docs.text:
Offset the surface of a mesh in or out with options for even thickness.

Re-using cutters

This can be useful when re-using the same mesh object to perform multiple cuts/operations.

Here we're using the same basic cutter to perform two cuts:

  • The base mesh has a bevel and is used for a Cut Groove modifier.
  • A linked duplicate is then using Offset Surface before the bevel then a Solidify Pro and is used for a Boolean Extrude modifier.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Distance: Distance to offset surface.
  • Even thickness: Method for even thickness.
  • Direction: Direction of offset:
    • Normal: Normal stored on geometry. Will use custom normals if they exist.
    • True Normal: Geometric normal (ignores custom normals).
    • Custom: Custom direction (Specify).

docs.title: Selection
docs.text: See selection settings.

docs.title: Project to Surface
docs.text:
Project and blend geometry onto other mesh surfaces. Transfer normals and UVs for a seamless blend.

Similar to Surface Insert but this modifier is added to the "decal/patch" mesh, not the main surface. It's the faster option if you don't need to weld the meshes together.

  • Blend a mesh object to other surfaces. Multiple other mesh surfaces can be specified.

  • Project mesh as a "Decal" onto other objects. This flattens the geometry but keeps the original normals.

Open Edges

This modifier works best on meshes with "open edges", i.e. non-solid objects. These edges are used as the base for most masking methods.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Be sure to check out the examples file to see Project to Surface in action.

docs.title: Projection Targets
docs.text:
Choose which meshes to project to.

  • Target Objects: How many mesh objects to project to.
  • Objects: Choose individual mesh objects to project to.
  • Collection: Choose a collection containing mesh objects to project to.

docs.title: Projection
docs.text:
Define how mesh is projected to surfaces.

  • Method: Method for vertex projection:
    • Wrap to Surface: Wrap mesh to target surface. Points will be projected to target surface and re-displaced based on their calculated height.
    • Blend with Surface: Project points to target surface then blend between original and projected positions.
    • Project Decal: Flatten geometry to target surface while keeping original normals. Ideal for "floaters" intended for baking.
  • Wrap Normals: Set normals based on interpolated surface normals. Gives better results.
  • Surface Offset: Move projected vertices a fixed amount towards or away from the target surface.
  • Decal Height: How much of the original mesh height to keep when using Project Decal. 0 is completely flat.

docs.title: Projection Direction
docs.text:
Control the direction and properties of surface projection.

  • Project Direction: Define direction of projection rays:
    • Object Direction: Direction in object space (default -Z).
    • World Direction: Direction in world space (default -Z).
    • Mesh Normal: Use individual point normals.
    • Mesh Island Normal: Use the average normal of each mesh island.
    • Mesh Tangent: Use individual point tangents.
    • Surface Normal: Use the normal of the closest part of target surface.
  • Base Height: How height is calculated for Wrap to Surface and Project Decal projection methods:
    • Boundary Center: Calculate height from a plane defined by the center of the boundary and the projection direction.
    • Object Origin: Calculate height from a plane defined by the objects origin and the projection direction.
  • Re-Displace: When using Wrap to Surface. Direction to apply calculated height:
    • Projection: Apply height displacement using the projection direction.
    • Surface Normal: Apply height displacement using the normal of the target surface.
  • Ray Length: Maximum distance rays will collide with target surface. Best to keep at a large enough value that all points collide.
  • No Hit: Change behavior of vertices when projection rays miss:
    • Unchanged: Do not move vertex.
    • Closest Surface to Max Dist: Move vertex to the maximum distance in ray direction then snap to closest point on target surface.

docs.title: Projection Masking
docs.text:
Control how projection is masked. See Mask Falloff.

  • Vertex Group: Choose a vertex group to project.

docs.title: Transfer Normals
docs.text:
Transfer normals from target surfaces. Internally this uses Normal Transfer. Normals are transferred after vertex projection, using the closest target surface.

  • Normal Domain: Whether normals are stored on points (smooth) or face corners (allows sharp edges).
  • Normal Masking: How to mask the normal transfer:
    • Projection Mask: Use the same mask used for vertex projection.
    • New Mask: Create a new mask using mask falloff.
  • Vertex Group: Limit all normal transfer to a vertex group.

docs.title: Transfer UVs
docs.text:
Transfer UVs from target surface.

  • UV Map From: Which UV Map to transfer from the surface.
  • UV Map To: Which UV Map to write to on this object.

docs.title: Solidify Pro
docs.text:
Solidify Pro offers several advantages to Blender's Solidify Modifier:

  1. Custom normal support.
  2. Edge loops.
  3. Custom profile control.
  4. Inset control.
  5. More creasing control on the rim.
  6. Match Boundary normals.
  7. UV settings.
  8. Front/Back/Rim exclusion/output attributes.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Be sure to check out the examples file to see Solidify Pro in action.

docs.title: Current Limitations
docs.text:
Not all the settings of Blender's native "Solidify" modifier have been replicated yet. The notable exclusions are:

  • Cannot solidify edges with more than two faces. This is possible with "Complex" mode in the native modifier.
  • Float control of Bevel Weight on the solidified edges. Existing bevel weights can be carried over to the rim using the Bevel Weights panel, or bevel weight can be set on/off by using the output attribute Boundary Edges. This attribute can then be specified in a subsequent bevel modifier.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Thickness: Thickness of solidify operation.
  • Offset: Offset the thickness from the center.
  • Direction: Direction to extrude:
    • Normal: Normal stored on geometry. Will use custom normals if they exist.
    • True Normal: Geometric normal (ignores custom normals).
    • Custom: Custom direction (Specify).
  • Even Thickness: Method for calculating even thickness. See even thickness settings for more information.

docs.title: Output Geometry
docs.text:
In this section you can choose which parts of the solidify operation to keep.

Offset Surface

If you only plan on keeping the front/back of the solidify operation, consider using Offset Surface as it's much faster.

docs.title: Inset
docs.text:
Inset the front or back faces from their boundary edge.

  • Amount: Distance to inset faces.
  • Edge Falloff: Falloff distance from the edge of the inset. Use to smooth errors at the edge of the inset.
  • Scale: Scale faces around their average position. More stable than insetting but can be harder to control.

docs.title: Rim Geometry
docs.text:
Control the shape of the geometry created along the rim.

  • Rim Profile: Shape of the rim profile:
    • Linear: Flat rim with even edge loops.
    • V-Shape: Specify an angle for a "v-shape" profile.
    • Round: Round profile with even edge loops.
    • Custom Curve: Provide a curve object to apply as a rim profile.
  • Invert: Invert the height of the profile.
  • Reverse: Reverse the profile curve (swap left/right).

docs.title: Profile Geometry
docs.text:
• Profile Height: How height is calculated along the rim profile:
    • Consistent: Rim profile is consistent height based on the specified thickness.
    • Relative: Rim profile will scale locally based on the distance between points.
    • Specify: Specify a value for profile height.

docs.title: Crease
docs.text: Apply crease values to the rim. - Front: Crease value to apply on the front boundary. - Back: Crease value to apply on the back boundary. - Rim Crease: Method for creasing perpendicular rim edges: - Edge Angle: Apply creases by edge angle. - Signed Edge Angle: Apply creases by convex/concave angles. - Vertex Crease: Use vertex crease values for edge creases. - Rim: Crease value to apply to selected rim edges.

docs.title: Bevel Weights
docs.text:
Control how existing bevel weights are handled. Bevel weights on the original mesh are kept on the front and back faces.

  • Edge Weight Name: Name of the edge bevel weight attribute (default bevel_weight_edge).
  • Rim Weights: How to set bevel weights on the rim edges:
    • None: No bevel weights on the rim.
    • Extend: (Default) Extend bevel weights from the boundary across the rim.
    • From Vertex Weights: Use vertex bevel weights to set the rim's edge weights.
  • Vert Weight Name: Name of the vertex bevel weight attribute (default bevel_weight_vert). Used by "From Vertex Weights".

docs.title: Normals
docs.text: Control normals and sharp edges. - Mark Sharp: Mark solidified edges sharp. - Profile Angle: Angle along the profile curve to mark sharp (along the rim). - Rim Angle: Angle to mark sharp across the rim. - Extend Sharpness: Extend sharp edges across the rim. - Match Boundary Normals: Match normals along the rim boundary. Requires at least one edge loop.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text: Specify material to use on rim, you can either set material by index or specify a material.

docs.title: UVs
docs.text: Choose whether and how to generate UVs on rim faces

docs.title: Selection
docs.text: Which faces to solidify. See selection settings for more information.

docs.title: Surface Insert
docs.text:
Seamlessly join insert meshes into the surface of a mesh. Unlike Project to Surface, this modifier is added to the main surface in order to be able to cut and weld the surface geometry.

An insert mesh can be thought of as a "decal", "patch" or "plug".

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Be sure to check out the examples file to see Project to Surface in action.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
There are two primary ways of performing the insert operation:

  • Wrap to Surface Warp geometry to match the underlying surface.
  • Blend to Surface Keep world position of geometry and blend to surface via masking. This allows you to keep flat surfaces inside the insert mesh.

The Surface Insert Modifier performs the following steps:

  1. Insert meshes are projected to surface geometry using one of the above methods.
  2. Normals, materials and UVs are transferred from the original surface to the insert meshes.
  3. The surface is cut and removed where insert mesh open edges are.
  4. Vertices are matched on both sides of the seam and welded.

Mesh Islands

Insert meshes are performed per mesh island. Only mesh islands with open edges will be cut and welded into the original surface.

  • Manifold (solid) mesh islands can be projected but won't affect the underlying surface geometry.
  • Mesh islands that miss a raycast will be skipped entirely and a warning will show on the modifier.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. A receiving mesh object. This will have the modifier on it.
  2. An insert mesh with open edges. This will be projected, cut and welded into the surface of the receiving mesh.
  3. Insert mesh cannot partially cut into surface, it has to be fully surrounded.

docs.title: Insert Meshes
docs.text:
This section specifies which meshes to insert.

  • Objects/Collection: Choose individual mesh objects or a collection containing mesh objects.
  • Object Count: How many mesh objects to insert (when in Objects mode).
  • Instances: How to handle instances in insert geometry:
    • Realize, Use Transforms: Realize instances and use their local transforms (if projection direction is "Insert Direction").
    • Realize, Ignore Transforms: Realize instances and use their parent insert object's transform (if projection direction is "Insert Direction").
    • Stick to Insert Mesh: Keep instances and maintain their relative position to the nearest insert geometry.

docs.title: Insert Mesh Projection
docs.text:
• Method: How to project the insert meshes to the underlying surface:

    • Wrap to Surface: Warp geometry to match the underlying surface.
    • Blend with Surface: Warp geometry to match the underlying surface.

  • Projection Direction: Which direction to project insert mesh(es).

    • Mesh Island Normal: Use average mesh island normal
    • Insert Direction: Specify a direction in the space of each insert object.
    • Object Direction: Specify a direction in the space of receiving object.

  • Base Height. Where to use as the origin of the insert object. This will affect how the objects height is calculated for re-projection.

    • Boundary Center: Use average position of mesh boundary.
    • Object Origin: Use insert mesh origin.

  • Height Offset. Offsets insert mesh away from surface by a specified height.

  • Ray Length. Maximum distance to cast projection rays. Keep this value high: all rays need to hit for a successful insert.

docs.title: Projection Masking
docs.text:
This section controls masking the projection of insert meshes to the surface. This is most useful when using Blend with Surface.

Controlling falloff is covered here

docs.title: Insert Mesh Normals
docs.text:
This section controls how much of the surface normals are transferred to the insert mesh. This is most useful when using Blend with Surface.

  • Normal Masking

    • Projection Mask. Use the same mask falloff as the projection
    • New Mask. Create a new mask for normals

  • Recalculate Blend Normals. Only available when using Blend with Surface. This will recalculate the normals on the blended portion of the insert mesh before transferring any from the surface.

  • Match Boundary Normals. When choosing New Mask this will make sure the boundary edge of the insert mesh matches the normals on the underlying surface. Turn off to create a hard edge.

If New Mask is chosen, the settings for the falloff will appear below. Controlling falloff is covered here

docs.title: Surface Boolean
docs.text:
This section controls how the surface is cut for the insert mesh. Turn off if you don't wish to merge surface, this will make the modifier act like Project to Surface. To avoid guess-work it's often best to tweak these settings when viewing the "Boolean Cutters" debug view.

  • Weld Surfaces. Welds vertices between the surface and insert mesh. Turning this off will leave them as separate mesh islands.
  • Weld Distance. Distance at which to weld vertices, this takes effect at several points during the process, not just the final weld between surface and insert mesh.
  • Triangulate Blend Polys: Triangulate ngons created between the original surface and insert geometry.
  • Cutting Edges: Edge group that, if present, will limit which edges will cut into the surface. By default all open edges will cut but you can use an edge group to specify edges.
  • Boolean Caps: How to generate Boolean end caps. This can allow for complex insert meshes:
    • Allow Holes: Allow insert geometry to have holes. E.g.A circular strip of mesh to make a panel line where the center remains the original surface.
    • Allow Tubes: Insert geometry joins the surface at multiple points. E.g. A handle that joins the surface in two places.
    • Flatten Insert Mesh: Flatten and use insert geometry as the Boolean end caps. Can break when there are overhangs but can handle curvature in tight spaces better than the other methods.
  • Boolean Extrusion. How far to extrude the cutter shape from the surface. You might need to increase this value if the insert mesh covers a large area of curvature. You can preview cutters in the Debug panel.
  • Boolean Offset. Offset the Boolean cutter outside the surface. This only effects the "top" of the cutter and will also help when an insert mesh covers a large area of curvature. You can preview cutters in the Debug panel.
  • Non-Manifold Solver. Which Boolean solver to use when surface mesh is not manifold. Keep this as Float for most situations.
    • Float. Faster and in a lot of cases more accurate when matching surface points.
    • Exact. Much slower and rarely better. Included "just in case" it helps in rare cases.

docs.title: Materials
docs.text:
This section controls how materials and UVs are transferred from the surface to the insert meshes

  • Transfer Surface Material. How to transfer materials from the surface to the insert mesh.

    • None. Don't transfer any materials.
    • Boundary Material. Transfer the material island(s) that touch open edges.
    • All. Overwrite all insert mesh materials with those on the surface.

  • Transfer Material UVs. Transfer UV Maps for the transferred materials.

  • UV Map. Which UV map to transfer.

docs.title: Debug
docs.text:
This section lets you inspect steps of the process if the modifier isn't behaving as expected.

  • View. Outputs geometry from different points in the node graph.

    Warning

    This changes the output of the graph, make sure to turn off when done inspecting.

    • None. Output standard result, no debugging.
    • Boolean Cutters. Output the shapes used to cut the surface.
    • Skipped Insert Islands. Output any mesh islands that did not project due to missed ray casts.
  • Debug Cutters
  • Debug Skipped Insert Islands

docs.title: Surface Project
docs.text:
Modifier Renamed

This modifier is now called Project to Surface.

docs.title: Symmetrize
docs.text:
Mirrors a mesh on a single axis. Similar to Blender's Mirror Modifier but with the following improvements:

  1. Correctly mirrors custom normals.
  2. Optional gizmo for displaying the symmetry plane and direction.
  3. Output attributes for mirrored faces and center points.
  4. Global space option without having to use another object.

docs.title: Current Limitations
docs.text:
• Limited to a single axis. This can easily be overcome by using another symmetrize modifier.
  • You can't edit the mirrored side when "On Cage" is turned on like with the default mirror modifier.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Symmetry Space: Coordinate space to use for symmetry.
    • Local: Symmetrize in object's local space (default mirror modifier behavior).
    • Global: Symmetrize in global space based on the world origin.
    • Object: Symmetrize using another objects position and rotation.
  • Axis: Which axis to symmetrize on, relative to the Symmetry Space.
  • Flip Axis: Reverse direction of symmetry operation.
  • Show Axis: Display location and direction of symmetry operation.
  • Clipping: Clip geometry on the mirrored side of the symmetry plane.
    • None: No Clipping. All geometry will be mirrored across the symmetry plane.
    • Snap Points: Points on the mirrored side will be snapped to the symmetry plane.
    • Cut Geometry: Geometry will be sliced on the symmetry plane.

docs.title: Merge Points
docs.text: Merge points by distance after symmetry operation.

docs.title: UVs
docs.text:
Options to flip and offset UVs.

  • UV Map: Name of UV Map to edit.
  • Flip U: Flip mirrored UVs horizontally.
  • Flip V: Flip mirrored UVs vertically.
  • Offset: Offset mirrored UVs.

docs.title: Center Normals
docs.text:
• Mark Sharp: Mark center edges as sharp based on angle.
  • Angle: Minimum angle for a sharp edge.
  • Unify Custom Normals: Face corner normals on center points will average. Sharp edges will be preserved. Only applies if custom normals exist on mesh.

docs.title: Bent Normals
docs.text:
Bent normals can improve how surfaces react to ambient lighting, especially in non-path-traced renderers such as game engines.

Usually bent normals are baked to a texture but this modifier will calculate bent normals directly on geometry. A cone of rays is cast from each point and the normals are sampled and averaged to find the average direction of ambient light.

  • Bent normals off Unnaturally dark shadows.

  • Bent normals on Fake bounce light added to shadow areas.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: • Factor. How much bent normals are mixed in with existing normals.

docs.title: Collision Geometry
docs.text:
Collide with other objects in the scene.

  • Object. Object to collide rays with.
  • Collection. Collection to collide rays with.

docs.title: Raycast
docs.text:
Control the distribution of rays used to calculate the bent normals.

  • Ray Count. How many rays are cast.
  • Ray Length. How long to cast each ray.
  • Cone Angle. The angle of the cone that rays are distributed in using a Fibonacci distribution.

docs.title: Face Weighted Normals
docs.text:
Calculate face weighted normals for a mesh. This is similar to Blender's built-in Weighted Normals Modifier but with some differences:

  • Selection Panel lets you limit weighted normals to a specific part of your mesh.
  • Options are designed to be more intuitive and easier to use.

  • Un-weighted normals

  • Weighted normals

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Normal Domain. Whether normals are stored on points (smooth) or face corners (allows sharp edges).
  • Weight. Derive normal weights from:
    • Face Area. Faces with larger area have more influence over normals.
    • Face Strength. Use the "Face Strength" attribute. Official Documentation
    • Attribute. Define an attribute to use for normal weighting.
  • Keep Sharp. Keep sharp edges on face corners.
  • Corner Angle Weights. Include corner angles in weighting. Produces better normals for non -quads.

docs.title: Area Weights
docs.text:
Have more control over area-weighted normals.

  • Area Bias. Bend normals towards faces with larger areas. 1 = Direct weight based on area. Higher values will weight more aggressively to larger areas.
  • Area Cutoff. Ignores normals from smaller faces. Cutoff is a percentage of face area compared to the largest connected face.

docs.title: Selection
docs.text: See Selection options.

docs.title: Lock Normals
docs.text:
Creates custom normals for a mesh if none exist. Can also be used to convert between "Free" and "Tangent Space" normals, see the Blender Docs.

Collapsing Meshes

Tangent Space normals make manual edits to geometry with custom normals much easier. Apply this modifier or use Add Custom Normals to achieve this.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Custom Normal Type: How to store custom normals:

    • Free: Store custom normals as simple vectors in the local space of the mesh. This is efficient and fast to evaluate but does not support deformation.
    • Tangent Space: Store normals in a deformation dependent custom transformation space. This method is slower, but can be better when subsequent operations change the mesh without handling normals specifically.

  • Normal Domain: When Custom Normal Type is set to Free:

    • Face Corner. Store normals on face corners, allows for sharp edges.
    • Point. Store normals on points, cannot have sharp edges.

docs.title: Normal Transfer
docs.text:
Transfer Normals from other mesh objects. This can be useful in a variety of situations:

  • Blend between meshes without affecting geometry.

  • Fix / smooth shading of bad topology. See also Smooth Normals and Boolean Pro

  • Create better shading for foliage cards.

  • Match normals of "floater" decals. See also Surface Project

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Examples can be found in the Normal Modifiers scene in the example file

docs.title: Options
docs.text: • Normal Domain. Whether normals are stored on points (smooth) or face corners (allows sharp edges).

docs.title: Transfer Geometry
docs.text:
Choose which meshes to transfer normals from.

  • Object Count. How many mesh objects to transfer normals from.
  • Objects. Choose individual mesh objects to transfer normals from.
  • Collection. Choose a collection containing mesh objects to transfer normals from.

docs.title: Transfer
docs.text:
• Method. How to sample the normal from target surface:

    • Closest Surface. Sample normal at closest target surface.
    • Project Object Direction. Raycast-sample target geometry in object space.
    • Project Island Normal. Raycast-sample target geometry along the average mesh island normal.
    • Project Source Normals. Raycast-sample target geometry along mesh normals of this object.
    • Project Target Normals. Raycast-sample target geometry and use the normal of the closest target surface.

  • Ray Length (Project Methods). Maximum length of raycast to target surface.

  • Direction (Project Object Direction Only). Direction in object space to raycast (default is -Z).

  • Automatic Masking. Mask falloff for transferring normals, see Mask Falloff

docs.title: Selection
docs.text: See Selection options.

docs.title: Repair Bevel Normals
docs.text:
Beveling a mesh with custom normals can lead to unexpected behavior. This tool identifies bevels and replicates Blender's "Harden Normals" functionality found on the bevel modifier.

  • Bevel with custom normals
  • Repaired Normals

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Be sure to check out the examples file to see Repair Bevel Normals in action.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Mesh object with beveled faces you wish to fix

  • (Recommended) Set Face Strength to "Affected" or "All" on the bevel modifier

docs.title: Bevel Detection
docs.text:
How to detect bevelled faces.

  • Face Strength. Recommended option. Requires setting face strength on bevel modifier to "Affected" or "All"

    • Sharp Bevel Edge. Apply sharp edges to bevel's outer edges.
    • Sharp Bevel Corners. Apply sharp edges to bevel's corners.

  • Face Area. Select bevels by their face area.

    • Max Bevel Area. Faces with area below this value will be treated as bevels

  • Attribute. Use an attribute or vertex group to select beveled faces.

docs.title: Mark Sharp
docs.text:
Optionally mark sharp edges within and around the bevel. Both options are off by default.

  • Bevel Loop Angle. Mark sharp within the bevel by face loop angle.
    • Loop Angle. Angle between face loops at which to mark sharp.
  • Bevel Boundary Angle. Mark sharp when the angle between the bevel and surrounding faces exceeds this angle. Useful for partial bevels that terminate on corners.
    • Boundary Angle. Angle between the bevel and surrounding faces at which to mark sharp.

docs.title: Area Weighting
docs.text:
For weighting normals inside the bevel. Available when Bevel Detection is set to Face Area or Attribute

  • Area Bias. Bend normals towards faces with larger areas. 1 = Direct weight based on area. Higher values will weight more aggressively to larger areas.
  • Area Cutoff. Ignores normals from smaller faces. Cutoff is a percentage of face area compared to the largest connected face

docs.title: Selection Panel
docs.text: See Selection options

docs.title: Repair Boolean Normals
docs.text:
This tool attempts to fix bad normals caused by Booleans. This is intended for destructively applied Booleans, for Boolean modifiers please consider using Boolean Pro as it provides much more accurate and consistent results.

  • Default Boolean Normals
  • Repaired Boolean Normals

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
1. Mesh object with destructive Booleans applied.
  2. Mesh is un-triangulated i.e. Boolean operations have created ngons.
  3. Mesh has sharp edges on Boolean seams.

Even if a mesh meets all these requirements it isn't 100% guaranteed to fix all it's normals

docs.title: Error Correct Distance
docs.text:
Welds vertices on the proxy mesh that normals are transferred from.

This can fix normal issues but will also introduce more issues as the value increases. There should be a sweet spot where there aren't any issues

docs.title: Selection Panel
docs.text: See Selection options

docs.title: How it Works
docs.text:
1. Splitting the mesh on sharp edges, producing a surface for each "normal island"
  2. Detecting points on the boundary that don't join to any edges inside the island
  3. Re-creating a version of each island without those points
  4. Transferring normals per newly created island back up to the unaltered geometry

docs.title: Repair Mirrored Normals
docs.text:
Mirroring a mesh with custom normals will not mirror the normals. This leads to incorrect normals on the mirrored geometry. This modifier can repair these normals by flipping them in the correct direction.

Symmetrize

Try the Symmetrize modifier instead for mirroring with custom normals.

  • Unmirrored Custom Normals
  • Mirrored Custom Normals

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Normal Domain: Whether normals are stored on points (smooth) or face corners (allows sharp edges)
  • Method: Choose which faces get mirrored normals:
    • Detect: Faces and axes will be determined automatically, this should work in most cases.
    • Side of Origin: Select and mirror normals based on axis and object origin.
    • Specify: Specify which faces to flip normals and which axes to flip them on.
  • Mirror Object: If using a mirror object, specify it here.

docs.title: Side of Origin
docs.text:
Flip normals for faces on the "mirrored" side. Use this method when using "Bisect" on a mirror modifier or when original geometry doesn't cross the mirror plane(s).

  • Recalculate Center Normals: Recalculate Normals for points at the center of specified axes.
  • Mirror Axis: Which axes to select and mirror normals on.
  • Flip Axis: Flip the direction of the selection of normals to mirror.

docs.title: Specify
docs.text:
Choose which faces have flipped normals and what axis to flip them on. Use when geometry is mirrored across both sides of the mirror plane(s) and "Bisect" is turned off.

  • Mirror Axis: Which axes to select and mirror normals on.
  • Selection: See Selection Options

docs.title: Smooth Normals
docs.text:
Smooth Normals will smooth mesh normals without smoothing mesh topology. This can be useful in a variety of situations.

  • Achieve good shading on difficult topology. (Pinched, uneven or distorted normals).

  • Simplify cel shading contours.

  • Smooth and/or completely flatten normal islands.

  • Mix smoothed point normals for a unique effect (cheap SSS shading).

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Be sure to check out the examples file to see Smooth Normals in action.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Normal Domain. Whether normals are stored on points (smooth) or face corners (allows sharp edges).
  • Keep Sharp. Keep edges marked as sharp when normals are on face corners.

docs.title: Smoothed Proxy Mesh
docs.text:
Generate a smoothed version of the mesh to transfer normals from. The mesh is split on sharp edges before smoothing, you can preview this mesh from the debug panel.

  • Transfer Method. How to transfer the normals from the smoothed mesh.
    • Closest Surface. Transfer normals from the closest point of the smoothed mesh.
    • Point Index. Transfer normals by their original point index.
  • Iterations. How many iterations of smoothing to perform.

docs.title: Smooth Normals
docs.text:
Controls methods of directly smoothing mesh normals.

  • Smooth Method. How to smooth normals:

    • None. Don't perform any direct normal smoothing.
    • Blur Normals. Fastest Method of smoothing at the cost of being less accurate and not preserving shape as well.
    • Smooth Normals. Iterative smooth function of normals. Slower than blur but can produce better results.

  • Smooth/Blur Iterations. How many iterations of smoothing to apply to normals.

  • Face Weight Influence. Cheap approximation of face weighted normals, lessens the contribution of smaller faces.

docs.title: Flatten Normal Islands
docs.text:
Calculate the average normal direction for entire normal islands (defined by sharp edges).

  • Amount. How much to blend to the completely flat island normals.

docs.title: Mix Point Normals
docs.text:
Mix in smoothed point normals. This can achieve a unique effect, somewhat like sub-surface scattering.

  • Amount. How much to blend to the smoothed point normals.
  • Blur Iterations. Perform blur iterations on the point normals.

docs.title: Selection
docs.text: See Selection options

docs.title: Auto-Flip Faces
docs.text:
Flipped faces on meshes can cause multiple issues. Traditionally you would check for flipped faces by using the the 'Face Orientation' overlay and resolve areas of flipped faces one by one.

This modifier will detect flipped faces and fix them automatically.

  • Faces Flipped
  • Faces Un-flipped

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Invert. Change direction of entire mesh from outside to inside
  • Hit Rate. Tune the detection of flipped faces. Higher values will detect more but increase the risk of false positives.

docs.title: Change Materials
docs.text:
Assign materials or material indices to face selections.

Up to 6 materials can be assigned per modifier. Selections can be driven by existing material/index or arbitrary vertex/face groups.

Many normalMagic mesh modifiers output attributes that work well with Change Materials.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: • Materials to Apply: The number of materials to apply. This will show a panel for each material with a checkbox to enable/disable.

docs.title: Material #
docs.text: The panel for each material assignment, contains two sub-panels: One for selecting faces and one for specifying the material/index.

docs.title: Selection
docs.text:
Choose which faces to apply a material to.

  • Face Group: Specify a vertex/face group to apply materials to.
  • Material: Select faces by a specific material.
  • Material Index: Select faces by their material index.
  • Invert: Invert selection

docs.title: Material
docs.text:
Which material to apply to selected faces.

  • Set: Whether to set a specific material or material index.
  • Material: Which specific material to apply.
  • Material Index: Which material index to apply.

docs.title: Instance Object
docs.text:
Instances another object (after modifiers) to replace or append to the current objects geometry. This can be particularly useful for re-using details.

Create duplicates of an object without needing to sync all modifier settings to the duplicates.

Append to and nest modular pieces. Such as these bolt inserts, these can be instanced themselves and used with Surface Insert on larger meshes.

Add-on

The normalMagic Add-on has instance operators to make working with this modifier easier:

  • Create a linked duplicate of an object(s), replace all modifiers with Instance Object
  • Select original object being instanced

See add-on docs for more information.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Object. Object to instance
  • As Instance. When turned off, will copy object's geometry. Turned on will instance the object Official Documentation
  • Replace / Append. Replace will replace current objects geometry with that of the instance. Append will keep geometry and append the instanced object with additional transform options.

docs.title: Transform Instance
docs.text: When appending the instance, these settings allow you to transform the instance relative to the objects origin.

docs.title: Mark Sharp
docs.text:
Mark Sharp will mark edges as sharp based on edge angle. This is similar to Blender's Smooth By Angle modifier but with extra options. There are options to remove and/or add custom normals.

  • Smooth By Angle One angle for all edges
  • Mark Sharp Separate angles for convex/concave edges

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Keep Existing: Keep edges already marked as sharp.
  • Angle Type:
    • Absolute Angle: Use a single angle regardless off convexity. This behaves like "Smooth By Angle".
    • Convex / Concave: Specify different angles depending whether edges are convex or concave.
    • Edge Creases: Mark creased edges as sharp.
    • Custom Normal Seams: Detect seams in custom normals and mark as sharp.
  • Remove Custom Normals: Will remove any custom normals from geometry and use default normal calculation from sharp edges.

docs.title: Shade Auto Smooth (First)
docs.text:
Pro Add-on

This operator is part of the normalMagic Add-on.

Found in the object right-click menu, above Shade Smooth. It can be hidden in the add-on's preferences.

Adds the Preferred Smooth Modifier (Mark Sharp or Smooth by Angle) at the start of the modifier stack, so shading is based on the original mesh before other modifiers add new edges. On a checkpoint it is added after the Instance Object modifier.

If the object already has one, it is moved to the start instead (Blender's "Smooth by Angle" is unpinned from the end of the stack).

  • Angle. Maximum face angle for smooth edges. Only applies to newly added modifiers.

docs.title: Sharp Edges to Attribute
docs.text:
Write edge and point attributes based on sharp edges or other arbitrary edge attributes.

  • Edge attributes can be used for:

    • Mark sharp edges as UV seams.
    • Add a bevel weight to sharp edges.
    • Detect sharp edges from custom normals and mark them as sharp.

  • Point attributes can be used for:

    • Creating a vertex group for selection in another modifier from sharp edges.
    • Expanding selection with or without a falloff.

docs.title: Sharp Edge Detection
docs.text:
How to specify edges to write to attribute(s)

  • Detect From Markup. Use smooth shading attributes to define sharp edges. This might miss sharp edges defined by custom normals.
  • Detect Custom. Detect sharp edges from normals. This will detect sharp edges created from custom normals but can have a small amount of error.
  • Tolerance (When "Detect Custom" is on). Change the normal angle difference at which edges will be marked as sharp.

docs.title: Expand Points
docs.text:
Expand point selection. Can be useful in Selection Panel of other modifiers.

  • Point Values. How selection is expanded:
    • Float. Each expansion gets a lower value creating a falloff.
    • Bool. Each expansion is set to 1.
  • Expand Iterations. How many edges to expand point selection.
  • Falloff (When Point Values are "Float"). Falloff of point selection. similar to mask falloff

docs.title: Output Attributes
docs.text: What to name Edge / Point attributes. Leaving blank will not write to any attributes.

docs.title: View Normals
docs.text:
View Normals creates geometry to visualize mesh normals on objects.

  • Normals will show up in object mode
  • Normal Colors are currently only available in Material Preview and Rendered viewport shading.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Length. The object-space length of displayed normals
  • Normal Domain. Display normals on:
    • Points. One line will be generated per point.
    • Face Corners. One line will be generated per face corner.
    • Faces. One line will be generated per face.
  • View. Specify which normal to visualize:
    • Normal. Display the normal stored on the geometry, custom normals will be included here.
    • True Normal. Display the normal defined by topology, custom normals will be ignored.
    • Attribute. Specify an arbitrary attribute to use.

docs.title: Style
docs.text:
This section defines how the normal line mesh is generated:

Line Display normals as a single line. This is the most efficient but can't be colored.

Cylinder / Tapered Cylinder Display Normals as mesh cylinders with a width and color that will show up in Material Preview and Rendered viewport shading

docs.title: Colors
docs.text:
(When in Cylinder / Tapered Cylinder mode)

  • Color. Color to display normals.

  • Show Default. Colors normals differently if they match default "Smooth Shading" normals:

docs.title: View Sharp
docs.text: View sharp generates geometry to visualize sharp edges on a mesh. Similar to View Normals colors are currently only available in Material Preview and Rendered viewport shading.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Detect Sharp. How to detect sharp edges:

    • From Markup. Use smooth shading attributes to define sharp edges. This might miss sharp edges defined by custom normals.
    • From Normals. Detect sharp edges from normals. This will detect sharp edges created from custom normals but can have a small amount of error.
    • Both. Combine both methods above to detect sharp edges.

  • Tolerance (When "From Normals" is used). Change the normal angle difference at which edges will be marked as sharp.

  • Width. Width of pipe geometry created in object-space.
  • Color. Color to apply to sharp edge visualization.
